body: AI-assisted classroom PR1 review, submitted using the reviewer B account like577. Reviewed the intentionally weak description, the single commit, and check status; read tests before implementation. Compared the pinned head with self-authored docs/review-checklist.md, docs/requirements/classroom-description.md, and the SPEC_ONLY OpenAPI reference. The pinned local suite passes 7 tests; GitHub has no check runs or status contexts, so no CI pass is claimed. Eight inline comments cover C1-C8, with two applicable suggestions and one question. No blocking functional defect was demonstrated; all changes are optional improvements. The HTTP adapter remains unimplemented. This COMMENT is not APPROVE, a merge, or teacher acceptance.

comments.body:
<!-- PR1-R01 -->
Location: `classroom-git/tests/test_description.py:9`.
Observation: The tests explicitly accept both inclusive limits, 10 and 500, while the next test rejects 9 and 501; this matches EX-DESC-03.
Impact: These neighbours protect against off-by-one regressions; the current implementation satisfies this requirement.
Proposal: Keep these exact boundary regressions when refactoring. No code change is requested for this item.
Label: [C2][verified][nonblocking]

<!-- PR1-R02 -->
Location: `classroom-git/tests/test_description.py:18`.
Observation: The trimmed minimum is covered, but padded inputs at the maximum (500 accepted, 501 rejected) are not directly tested.
Impact: A future length-before-strip change could reject a valid 500-code-point description without the present trim test detecting the upper-bound regression.
Proposal: Extend this test with both padded boundaries and the padded invalid upper neighbour (EX-DESC-02/03); this is added regression coverage, not a demonstrated current bug.
Label: [C3][test][nonblocking]

```suggestion
        for size in (10, 500):
            with self.subTest(trimmed_length=size):
                self.assertEqual(validate_description(" \t" + "x" * size + "\r\n"), "x" * size)
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            validate_description(" \t" + "x" * 501 + "\r\n")
```

<!-- PR1-R03 -->
Location: `classroom-git/tests/test_description.py:29`.
Observation: Chinese/Russian examples exercise non-ASCII text, but they do not distinguish Unicode code points from UTF-16 units or visible grapheme clusters.
Impact: Cross-language ports or UI counters could silently change the documented EX-DESC-03 length unit.
Proposal: Add ten supplementary-plane symbols and five two-code-point combining sequences; both contain ten Python code points and should be accepted.
Label: [C5][unicode][test][nonblocking]

```suggestion
        for value in ("中" * 10, "Описание заявки", "😀" * 10, "e\u0301" * 5):
```

<!-- PR1-R04 -->
Location: `classroom-git/tests/test_description.py:23`.
Observation: The invalid-type table covers None, numbers, bool, lists and bytes; mapping-shaped inputs are not listed.
Impact: A JSON request body can supply an object where a string is expected; an explicit dictionary case would document the same TypeError contract for that common caller mistake.
Proposal: Optionally add a dictionary such as {"description": "valid description"} to this table. The current isinstance check already rejects it; no current defect is asserted (EX-DESC-01).
Label: [C4][test][nonblocking]

<!-- PR1-R05 -->
Location: `classroom-git/exercise.py:12`.
Observation: The docstring identifies normalization and code-point length, but does not describe the two exception categories visible below.
Impact: Callers must read implementation details to distinguish wrong input types from invalid normalized lengths, reducing traceability to EX-DESC-01/03.
Proposal: Optionally expand the docstring with TypeError and ValueError cases and reference the standalone-function scope. Preserve the intentionally weak initial PR description during this classroom stage.
Label: [C1][documentation][nonblocking]

<!-- PR1-R06 -->
Location: `classroom-git/exercise.py:14`.
Observation: This branch raises TypeError directly and has no HTTP adapter; docs/api/classroom-openapi.yaml is explicitly SPEC_ONLY and outside this PR's implementation scope.
Impact: Treating this function as a running API would misstate both delivery status and transport-level error handling.
Proposal: Can we confirm that a future adapter, rather than this validator, will map TypeError to 422/invalid_type and ValueError to 422/invalid_length as described in the reference contract? No endpoint is requested in this PR (EX-DESC-05).
Label: [C6][question][scope][nonblocking]

<!-- PR1-R07 -->
Location: `classroom-git/exercise.py:15`.
Observation: strip() creates the normalized value without external writes or logging, consistent with EX-DESC-02/04; internal content is not rewritten.
Impact: Keeping normalization local preserves callers' original data and avoids exposing submitted descriptions through debug logs.
Proposal: Retain this pure boundary and consider a regression assertion with internal spaces, e.g. validate_description("ab cd ef gh") == "ab cd ef gh". No logging or extra sanitization is needed here.
Label: [C7][verified][maintainability][nonblocking]

<!-- PR1-R08 -->
Location: `classroom-git/exercise.py:17`.
Observation: The failure message says 'characters', while the function docstring and EX-DESC-03 define Unicode code points after trimming.
Impact: Users reading a combining-sequence error may interpret a character as a displayed glyph, creating avoidable diagnostic ambiguity even though the calculation is correct.
Proposal: Optionally say '10 to 500 Unicode code points after trimming' in the ValueError message; preserve its exception class and acceptance rules.
Label: [C8][nit][diagnostics][nonblocking]
